subject: Call recap + cost guardrails and host-comparison follow-up (PulseHealth pilot)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Call recap + cost guardrails and host-comparison follow-up (PulseHealth pilot)

Hi Aisha — great to speak earlier. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we can move to a pilot scope quickly.

Summary of discovery (from our call):
- Expected steady-state volume: ~200–300M tokens / month after ramp (peak on analytics jobs).
- Token mix: ~35% short prompt (≤256 tokens), ~65% long/chain-of-thought outputs (avg 1,200 tokens).
- Primary worries: predictable unit cost, tail latency on larger sequences, and audit logs for model outputs.

Pulse requests / asks we captured:
1) A target range for unit economics: what $/1M tokens you expect as an acceptable target for procurement.
2) A pilot pricing proposal that protects your budget while we prove quality and latency SLOs.
3) Evidence of comparative unit cost vs major hosts (OpenAI/Anthropic) for the same effective workload.

Initial benchmarking notes (high level) — these are ballpark effective costs for comparable model families and workload shapes (includes batching/kv-cache assumptions):
- OpenAI (API): ~ $55–75 / 1M tokens (higher for long-sequence models/LLMs with state retention).
- Anthropic (API): ~ $50–70 / 1M tokens (varies by model family).
- Self-hosted / optimized open-model providers (aggressive quant + batching): ~ $25–45 / 1M tokens.
- Redwood illustrative target for this workload (dependent on batching & quantization profile): $28–38 / 1M tokens for production pilot if we commit to caching + batching policy.

Next steps we discussed (action items):
- Aisha: confirm a firm monthly token estimate (conservative and aggressive view) — attachment: PulseHealth_token_profile_20261003.xlsx.
- Ben (me): deliver a 90-day pilot proposal with a proposed $/1M rate band, commit tiers, and SLOs (including latency targets for long sequences).
- Redwood: include a short comparatives sheet (redwood_rate_sheet_1M_comparisons.pdf) that shows effective per-1M math and assumptions.

If you can confirm the two token scenarios (base vs peak) by Monday, I’ll fast-track a pilot quote and a one-page commercial term sheet for legal/procurement to review.

Thanks — enjoyed the conversation.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment stubs: PulseHealth_token_profile_20261003.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_rate_sheet_1M_comparisons.pdf (pdf)
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@pulsehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: PulseHealth Procurement <procurement@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2026 17:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Call recap + cost guardrails and host-comparison follow-up (PulseHealth pilot)

Ben — thanks for the fast recap. Confirming the numbers from our side and adding procurement context.

Confirmed token profile (quick):
- Conservative: 160M tokens / month (first 3 months of pilot).
- Expected ramp: 250M tokens / month by month 6 (after feature rollouts).
- Peak/seasonal: up to ~420M tokens in heavy-analysis weeks.

Budget guidance (procurement):
- We have a monthly budget band for model costs of $9k–$15k for the pilot stage. Procurement prefers not to exceed $15k/month on the initial term.

Target unit request: procurement would be comfortable with a pilot-level committed rate of $30–$45 per 1M tokens provided SLOs and a short-term cap that avoids overrun surprises.

Please include in the proposal:
- A clear overage model and a fail-safe cap option.
- Proof points on long-sequence latency and whether KV-cache helps materially.
- Any migration credits or trial credits you can extend for the first 90 days.

I'll attach a short token-export from our staging logs (separate email). We can sign off once legal sees a one-page term summary and the pilot pricing.

Thanks,
Aisha
Director of Product — AI, PulseHealth
aisha.khan@pulsehealth.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 04 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: recommended pilot structure for PH-2026-045 (notes)

Ben / Marissa — quick internal note after reading Aisha’s budget band. Suggested pilot commercial that balances cost visibility and ability to prove economics: 

Proposal sketch we should push:
- Pilot term: 90 days, capped commitment: 300M tokens total (protects PulseHealth) with monthly smoothing (min 80M/month in months 1–3).
- Intro rate: $34 / 1M tokens for the first 90 days (applies to committed usage up to 300M).
- Overage: $48 / 1M beyond committed 300M during pilot (gives runway for bursts).
- Ramp pricing: if PulseHealth converts to a 12-month committed plan within 60 days of pilot start, retroactively apply $30 / 1M for pilot usage and provide one-month free migration credits (to offset integration costs).

Justification / notes on numbers:
- $34 initial gives them a midpoint inside their $30–45 target while keeping us at healthy unit economics when using aggressive batching + KV cache on long sequences (we model savings of ~25–35% vs naïve per-token run).
- Overage at $48 disincentivizes uncontrolled burst cost but keeps procurement comfortable compared to API list rates.

Action items for me: draft one-page commercial term sheet + short appendix showing the per-1M math (assumptions: avg 1200-token output, 1.3x input inflation for system prompts, 30% effective batching improvement).

Priyom
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, PulseHealth Procurement <procurement@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot proposal & next steps — PulseHealth (90-day pilot, proposed rates)

Hi Aisha / team — appreciate the quick confirmation on volumes and budget. Per our internal conversation, attached is a 1-page commercial sketch and an illustrative rate sheet. Key points below so procurement has a single place to reference.

Pilot commercial summary (proposal):
- Term: 90 days.
- Commitment: 300M tokens total (monthly smoothing; min 80M/month first 3 months).
- Intro committed rate: $34 / 1M tokens (applies up to 300M commitment).
- Overage rate (pilot): $48 / 1M tokens beyond the 300M cap during pilot.
- Conversion sweetener: sign a 12-month commitment within 60 days and we retro-apply $30 / 1M to pilot usage + one month free migration credits.

Why this is competitive vs major hosts (concise):
- OpenAI/Anthropic APIs: list effective costs for similar long-sequence work often sit above $50 / 1M once you account for model family, long outputs, and lack of aggressive KV-caching.
- Self-hosted open-model providers can hit low $20s / 1M but require infra + ops investment (and often have higher tail latencies).
- Redwood aim: deliver mid-$20s–low-$30s / 1M effective cost through batching, KV cache, and model selection while keeping SLA, tooling, and secure telemetry (so you don’t take on infra ops).

Operational SLOs we’ll include with the pilot:
- 95th percentile latency target for long sequences (<= 800ms token-generation latency for 95th on typical analytics sequences) — we’ll baseline in the first 2 weeks.
- Audit logs and retention: 90-day query logs available for review; Enterprise options if you need longer retention.

Next steps we propose:
1) PulseHealth: confirm acceptance of pilot commercial sketch or propose a tweaked committed token amount.
2) Redwood Legal: we’ll send a one-page term summary and a simple SOW for the pilot.
3) Tech sync: schedule a 30–45 minute ops call (Priyom + Redwood infra lead) to map integration and instrumentation.

I’ll attach the two files we referenced in the thread and will follow with the term sheet before end of day. If you want to tighten the committed volume down or split the pilot into two milestones, we can do that — just say the word.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: PulseHealth_token_profile_20261003.xlsx, redwood_rate_sheet_1M_comparisons.pdf
